translations.text: Paul, called apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother,
to the church of God which is in Corinth, to those sanctified by Christ Jesus, called saints, together with all who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, theirs and ours:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I always give thanks to my God for you, for the grace of God given to you by Christ Jesus.
For in everything you were made rich in him, in every word and in all knowledge,
just as the testimony of Christ was confirmed among you,
so that you may lack nothing, not in a single grace, and may await the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ.
He will also establish you until the end, blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
God is faithful, by whom you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

Now I beseech you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all say the same thing, and let there be no division among you, but be firmly established in the same mind and in the same knowledge.
For it has been made known to me about you, my brothers, by those of Chloe's people, that there are some quarrels among you.
Now I say this because each one of you says: "I am of Paul," and "I am of Apollos," and "I am of Cephas," and "I am of Christ."
Is Christ divided? Or was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
I give thanks to God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
so that no one may say: "I baptized in my own name."
Now I also baptized the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.
For Christ did not send me to baptize but to preach the gospel, not with wisdom of speech, so that the cross of Christ may not be made empty.
For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
For it is written: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the knowledge of the knowledgeable I will bring to contempt."
Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the investigator of this world? Has God made foolish the wisdom of this world?
For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through its own wisdom, God saw fit, through the preaching of foolishness, to save those who believe.
For the Jews ask for a sign, and the Gentiles seek wisdom.
But we preach Christ crucified: to the Jews indeed a stumbling block and to the Gentiles foolishness.
But to those who are called, both Jews and Gentiles, Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God.
For the foolish thing of God is wiser than men, and the weak thing of God is stronger than men.
For consider your calling, brothers: not many are wise according to the flesh, are they? Not many are mighty, are they? Not many are noble, are they?
Instead, God chose the foolish things of the world to put the wise to shame, and God chose the weak things of the world to put the mighty to shame.
And God has chosen the ignoble of the world and the despised, and the things that are not, so that he might bring to nothing the things that are.
so that no flesh may boast before God.
From him you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, righteousness and holiness and redemption,
so that, as it is written: Let him who boasts, boast in the Lord.
And I, when I came to you, brothers, did not come with superiority of speech or of wisdom to tell you the testimony of God.
For I resolved in my heart to make known to you nothing else except Christ Jesus, and him crucified.
And I was with you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling.
And my word and my preaching were not by the persuasion of words of human wisdom, but by the manifestation of the Spirit and of power,
so that your faith might not rest on the wisdom of men, but on the power of God.
Yet I speak wisdom among the perfect, but not the wisdom of this world, nor of the rulers of this world, who are passing away,
but I speak the wisdom of God, the hidden mystery, which God foreordained before the ages for our glory,
which none of the rulers of this world knew; for if they had known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
But as it is written: What eye has not seen, and ear has not heard, and what has not entered the heart of man, what God has prepared for those who love him.
But to us God has revealed it through his Spirit; for the Spirit searches out everything, even the depth of God.
For who among men knows what belongs to a man, except the man's own spirit, which is in him? So too no one knows what belongs to God, except the Spirit of God.
But we have received not the spirit of this world, but the Spirit that is from God, so that we may know what has been granted to us by God;
which things we also speak, not with the learning of words of human wisdom, but with the teaching of the Holy Spirit, matching spiritual things to spiritual people.
But the natural man does not accept what belongs to the Spirit of God, for it seems foolishness to him, and he is not able to understand it, because it is spiritually judged.
But the spiritual person judges everything, and he himself is judged by no one.
For who has known the mind of the Lord, so as to counsel him? But we have the mind of Christ.
And I, brothers, could not speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to fleshly people, as to infants in Christ.
I gave you milk to drink and not solid food, for you were not yet able to take it, and even now you are still not able,
for you are still fleshly. For where there is still envy and strife among you, are you not still fleshly and behaving in a merely human way?
For when someone says: I belong to Paul, and another says: I belong to Apollos, are you not still fleshly?
For what is Paul? Or what is Apollos? Only servants, through whom you believed, and each as the Lord granted to him.
I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.
So then neither the one who plants is anything, nor the one who waters, but God who gives the growth.
But the one who plants and the one who waters are one; and each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
For we are God's fellow workers; you are God's workmanship and God's building.
By the grace of God given to me, like a wise master builder I laid the foundation, and another is building on it. But let each one take care how he builds.
For no one can lay another foundation apart from the one that has been laid, which is Jesus Christ.
If anyone builds on this foundation with gold, silver, precious gems, wood, hay, or reed,
each one's work will be made manifest, for that day will reveal it, because it is to be revealed by fire; and the fire will test each one's work, of what sort it is.
He whose work that he has built remains will receive a reward.
He whose work is burned up will suffer loss; but he himself will be saved, and saved in this way, as if from fire.
Do you not know that you are temples of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells among you?
Whoever destroys the temple of God, God will destroy him also; for the temple of God is holy, and that is what you are.
Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you thinks himself wise in this world, let him become foolish, so that he may be wise.
For the wisdom of this world is madness before God, for it is written: He who catches the wise in their craftiness.
And again it says: The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are vain.
Therefore let no one boast of men, for all things are yours:
whether Paul, or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or the present time, or the time to come, all things are yours.
And you are Christ's, and Christ is God's.
Let a man regard us in this way: as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
Moreover, from here on it is required among stewards that one be found trustworthy.
But for me it is a very small thing if I am judged by you or by any human day; indeed, I do not even judge myself.
For I am aware of nothing against myself, yet I am not justified by this; the one who judges me is the Lord.

Therefore do not judge anything before the time, until the Lord comes, who will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and make manifest the counsels of hearts, and then each one's praise will come from God.

These things, brothers, I have applied as a pattern to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that you may learn from us not to think beyond what is written, so that you may not be puffed up against one another on account of a neighbor.
For who judges you? Or what do you have that you have not received? And if you have received it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?
Already you are sated, and already you have become rich, and without us you have reigned. And would that you did reign, so that we too might reign with you!
For I think that God has displayed us apostles last of all, like men condemned to death, for we have become a spectacle to the world, and to angels, and to men.
We are fools for Christ's sake, but you are wise through Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are glorious, but we are dishonored.
To this very hour we both hunger and thirst, we are naked and are beaten, we are without rest, and we toil,
For we labor with our own hands. Those who revile us we bless; we are persecuted and we endure;
those who slander us we pray for; we have become like the refuse of the world, the offscouring of all until now.
I do not write this to shame you, but I instruct you as my beloved children.
For even if you have ten thousand tutors in Christ, yet you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus, through the gospel, I begot you.
I beg you, be imitators of me.
For this reason I have sent to you Timothy, who is my beloved son and faithful in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ, just as I teach in every place in all the churches.
So that, at my not coming to you, some have become arrogant.
But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the talk of those arrogant people, but their power,
for the kingdom of God is not in word, but in power.
What do you wish? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?
It is heard everywhere [?] that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not even named among the Gentiles: that someone should have his father's wife as his wife.
And you are arrogant, and have you not rather mourned, so that he who did this deed might be removed from among you?
For though I am far away in body, yet I am near in spirit; and I have already reckoned, as one present there, concerning such a man who did that deed,
in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, at the gathering of my spirit and yours, together with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,
to hand such a man over to torment in the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved on that day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
That boasting of yours is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole mixture?
Therefore cleanse out that old leaven, so that you may be a new batch of dough, just as you are unleavened; for Christ was slaughtered for us as our Passover.
So let us keep the Passover not with that old leaven, nor with the leaven of evil and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of righteousness and truth.
I wrote to you in this letter: do not associate with fornicators;
and not with all the fornicators of this world, or the greedy, or robbers, or idolaters; otherwise, you would have to go out of the world.

But now I have written to you: do not associate with anyone who is called a brother if he is a fornicator or greedy, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or a robber; with such a person do not even eat.
For what business of mine is it to judge those outside? Do you not judge those inside?
But God will judge those outside; and remove that wicked person from among you.
Does anyone among you who has a case against his neighbor dare to go to judgment before liars, and not rather before the saints?
Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you not worthy of that contemptible court?
Do you not know that we shall judge angels, let alone the things of this world?
If you have any court concerning this world, do you seat those who are despised in the congregation, these people?
I say this to you to shame you: is there no one among you so wise who could judge between him and his brother?
But brother goes to judgment with brother, and this before unbelievers.
Now therefore this is already an utter defeat for you, that you have lawsuits with one another. Why do you not rather suffer wrong? Why are you not rather defrauded?
But you do wrong and defraud, and this to brothers.

Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor effeminate men, nor men who lie with men, nor the greedy,
nor thieves, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor robbers will inherit the kingdom of God.
And such you once were; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.
All things are lawful for me, but not all things are beneficial; all things are lawful for me, but I will not submit to the authority of anything.
Food is for the belly and the belly for food; but God will bring to nothing both the one and the other. Yet this body is not for fornication, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
And God both raised up the Lord and will raise us up by his power.
Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take away the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? May it not be!
Do you not know that whoever joins himself to a prostitute, they are one body? For it says: The two shall be one flesh.
But whoever joins himself to the Lord is one spirit with him.
Flee fornication. Every sin that a person commits is outside the body; but whoever fornicates sins against his own body.
Do you not know that your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit within you, which you have from God, and that you do not belong to yourselves?
For you were bought with a price. Glorify God therefore with your body, which is God's.
Now concerning what you wrote to me: it is better for a man not to touch a woman at all.
But because of fornication, let each man have his own wife, and let each woman have her own husband.
Let the husband give his wife what is due to her, and likewise the wife to her husband.
The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband does; and likewise the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife does.

Do not separate from one another, except perhaps by agreement, for a certain time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer and fasting; and then be together with one another again, so that the devil may not tempt you through your lack of self-control.
But I say this as a concession, not as a command.
For I wish that every person were as I myself am; but each one has his own gift from God, one in this way and another in that way.
I say to the unmarried and to the widows: it is good for them if they remain thus, as I do.
But if they cannot exercise restraint, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.
And to the married I give command, not I, but the Lord: a wife is not to separate from her husband.
But if she does separate, let her remain unmarried, or else stay with her own husband; and let the husband not leave his wife.
And to the rest I say, I and not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she consents to live with him, let him not leave that wife.
And if a woman has an unbelieving husband, and it seems right to him to be with her, let her not leave that husband.
For the unbelieving husband is sanctified by the believing wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the believing husband; otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
But if the unbeliever separates, let him separate; the brother or the sister is not enslaved in such matters, for God has called us to peace.
For what do you know, woman, whether you will save your husband? Or what do you know, man, whether you will save your wife?
But as God has apportioned to each one, and as the Lord has called each one, so let them walk. And thus I command all the churches.
If anyone was called circumcised, let him not be troubled; if anyone was called uncircumcised, let him not be circumcised.
Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is likewise nothing, but what matters is keeping the commandments of God.
Let each one remain in that calling in which he was called.
If you were called as a slave, let nothing trouble you; but even if you are able to be set free, strive for it all the more.
For whoever is called by the Lord as a slave has been set free by the Lord; likewise the free man who is called is a slave of Christ.
You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men.
Brothers, let each one remain before God in that state in which he was called.
Now concerning virgins I have no command from the Lord; but I give advice as one who has received mercy from the Lord to be trustworthy.
I think, then, that this is good because of the distress that has come upon us, for it is better for a person to remain as he is.
If you are bound to a wife, do not divorce her. If you are free from a wife, do not seek a wife.
If you marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Such people will take upon themselves affliction of the flesh; but I am sparing you.
But this I tell you, brothers: this time has been shortened from now on; so that those who have wives should be as though they did not have them;
and those who weep, as though they did not weep; and those who rejoice, as though they did not rejoice; and those who buy, as though they did not possess;
and those who make use of this world, as though they did not make use of it, for the form of this world is passing away.
And I want you to be free from care. The unmarried man cares for the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord,
but the married man cares for the things of the world, how he may please his wife.

The woman and the virgin are also divided. The unmarried woman cares for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit; but the married woman cares for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
This I say for your own benefit, not to lay a snare for you, but so that you may stand before the Lord in a seemly and good way, free from care.
If anyone considers his virginity shameful, if it is past its time, and it seems right to him that it should be so, let him do what he wishes; he does not sin. Let them marry.
But he in whose heart it is firmly established, who has no distress, who has authority over his own will, and who has determined in his heart to keep his virginity, does well.
And whoever gives his virginity in marriage does well; but whoever does not marry does better.
A woman is bound by the law for as long as her husband is alive. But if that husband dies, she is free, if she wishes to marry, but only in the Lord.
But she is more blessed if she remains as she is, according to my counsel. And I think that I have the Spirit of God.
Now concerning things sacrificed to idols, we know, for we all have knowledge. We have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
If anyone thinks that he knows something, he has not yet known as one ought to know.
But whoever loves God is known by him.
Now concerning the eating of food offered to idols, we know that no idol is anything in the world, and that there is no other God, but only the one God.
For even if there are some so-called gods, whether in the heavens or on earth, as there are many gods and many lords,
yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and we are directed toward him; and there is one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we are through him.
But knowledge is not in everyone. Some, with misgiving even until now about the idol, eat the food as something offered to an idol, and their weak mind is defiled.
Food will not bring us before God. For if we eat, nothing is added to us, and if we do not eat, nothing is lacking to us.
But take care lest this authority of yours become a stumbling block to the weak.
For if someone sees you, who have knowledge, sitting [?] in an idol's temple, will not the mind of that weak person be built up to eat the food offered to idols?
And that weak brother, for whom Christ died, will perish through your knowledge.
When you sin in this way against the brothers and strike their weak mind, you sin against Christ.
Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat, so that I may not cause my brother to stumble.
Am I not an apostle? Am I not free? Have I not seen our Lord Jesus Christ with my eyes? Are you not my work in the Lord?
Even if I am not an apostle to others, yet to you at least I am, for you are the seals of my apostleship in the Lord.
This is my defense to those who judge me.
Do we not have the authority to eat and to drink?
Do we not have the authority to take sisters, wives, about with us, as the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas do?
Or is it only I and Barnabas who have no right to work?
Who ever serves as a soldier [?] at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat of its fruit? Or who tends a flock and does not eat of the milk of the flock?
Do I say this merely in a human way? Does not the law also say the same?
For it is written in the law of Moses: You shall not bind the mouth of the threshing ox. Is it about oxen that God is concerned?
Surely he speaks for our sake, for it was written for our sake. For the plowman ought to plow in hope, and the one who threshes in that same hope, to gather in hope.
If we have sown spiritual things among you, is it a great thing if we reap material things from you?

If others receive from your means by right, should we not do so all the more? But we did not wish for this right, for we endure everything, so that we may put no obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ.
Do you not know that those who serve the temple eat from the temple? And that those who stand before the altar receive a portion from the altar?
So also the Lord commanded that those who proclaim the gospel should have their living from the gospel.
But I have made use of none of these things. And I have not written this so that it may be so in my case. For it is better for me to die than that anyone should make my boast void.
For if I preach the gospel, that is no boast for me, for compulsion lies upon me, and woe to me if I do not preach the gospel.
For if I do this willingly, I have a reward; but if unwillingly, a stewardship has been entrusted to me.
What then is my reward? That when I preach the gospel, I preach the gospel of Christ free of charge, so that I make no use of my right in my preaching of the gospel.
For I was free of all, yet I made myself a slave to all, so that I might win the more.
Among the Jews I became as a Jew, so that I might win Jews; among those under the law as one under the law, so that I might win those under the law;
among the lawless as one lawless (I was not lawless toward God, but under the law of Christ), so that I might win the lawless;
among the weak I became as one weak, so that I might win the weak; I became all things to all, so that I might save all.
And this I do for the sake of the gospel, so that I may become a sharer in it.
Do you not know that those who run in the stadium all run, but one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may get there first.
And every competitor endures everything: they indeed in order to receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable one.
So I now run in this way, not as one running obscurely; I struggle in this way, not as one beating the air.
But I discipline my body and bring it into subjection, lest perhaps, after preaching to others, I myself should be found unproven.
I do not want you to be ignorant, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea.
And all were baptized by Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
and all ate the same spiritual food;
and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and that rock was Christ.
But God was not pleased with many of them, for they fell in the wilderness.
And these things became types for us, so that we might not be desirers of evil, as they desired.
Do not become idolaters, as some of them did, as it is written: The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to sing.
Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed fornication, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
Neither let us put the Lord to the test, as some of them tested him and perished by serpents.
Neither let us murmur, as some of them murmured and perished by the destroyer.
All these things happened to them as types; and they were written down for the instruction of us, upon whom the end of the times has come.
Therefore let anyone who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall.

No temptation has befallen you except what is human; but God is faithful, who will not let you be tempted beyond your strength, but with the temptation will also make a way out, so that you may be able to endure.
Now therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
I speak to you as to wise people; judge for yourselves what I say to you:
This cup of blessing which we bless, is it not a communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not a communion of the body of Christ?
For we who are many are one bread and one body, for we all partake of that one bread.
Consider Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices partakers of the altar?
What then am I saying by this, that an idol is anything, or that what is sacrificed is anything?
But I say that what the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I do not want you to be partakers with demons.
You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you cannot partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.
Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we perhaps stronger than he?
All things are lawful for me, but not all things are better; all things are lawful for me, but not all things build up.
Let no one seek only his own good, but each one also that of his neighbor.
Whatever is sold in the meat market, eat, and do not judge anything on account of conscience,
for the earth and its fullness are the Lord's.
And if one of the unbelievers invites you and you wish to go, eat everything set before you and do not judge anything on account of conscience.
But if someone says to you, "This is food offered to idols," do not eat, for the sake of the one who informed you and of conscience, for the earth and its fullness are the Lord's.
I speak of conscience, not your own but your neighbor's. For why is my freedom judged by another's conscience?
If I eat with thanksgiving, why am I reviled for that for which I give thanks?
Whether you eat, or whether you drink, or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.
Give no offence to Jews, to Gentiles or to the churches of God,
Just as I in all things please everyone, for I do not seek what is better for myself, but for the many, so that they may be saved.
Become imitators of me, as I am of Christ.
And I praise you, brothers, because you remember everything of mine, and you have kept the teaching just as I delivered it to you.
And I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, and the head of a woman is her husband, and the head of Christ is God.
Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered shames his head.
And every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered shames her head; for it is one and the same as one who is shaved.
For if a woman does not cover herself, let her also be shorn; but if it is shameful for a woman to be shorn or shaved, let her cover herself.
A man therefore ought not to cover his head, for he is the image and glory of God, but woman is the glory of her husband.
For man is not from woman, but woman from man;
and man was not created for woman's sake, but woman for man's sake.
For this reason a woman ought to have authority over her head, because of the angels.
But neither is man without woman, nor woman without man, by the Lord.
For just as woman is from her husband, so also the husband [?] for the sake of his wife; but all things are from God.
Judge this among yourselves: is it fitting for a woman to pray before God uncovered?
Does not nature itself teach you that if a man lets his hair grow long, it is a disgrace to him?
But if a woman lets her hair grow long, it is a glory to her, for the hair has been given to her as an adornment.
But if anyone is contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God.
In instructing you in this, I do not praise you, for you come together not for the better but for the more deficient.
First, then, I hear that when you gather as a church there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.
For there must also be divisions among you, so that those among you who are chosen may become evident.
So when you gather together, it is not a church for the eating of bread.
For each one takes his own supper ahead of time to eat, and someone is drunk.
Do you not have houses to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the church of God and shame those who have nothing? What should I say to you? Should I praise you for this? I do not praise you.
For I received from the Lord what I also gave to you: that the Lord Jesus Christ, on the night on which he was being handed over, took bread.
He gave thanks, broke it and said: Take and eat; this is my body, broken for you; do this in remembrance of me.
Likewise also the cup after supper, and he said: This cup is the new covenant of my blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me.
For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the death of the Lord until he comes.
Therefore, whoever eats this bread and drinks this cup of the Lord unworthily is guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
Let a person examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of that cup.
But whoever eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks to his own condemnation, because he did not discern the body of the Lord.
For this reason many among you are weak and sick, and many are lying down.
For if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged.
But when we are judged, we are disciplined by the Lord, so that we may not be condemned with the world.
Therefore, my brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
But if anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that you may not come together for condemnation. As for the rest, I will give instructions when I come.
Now concerning spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be ignorant.
You know that when you were pagans, you were led astray, following after those voiceless idols as you were led.
For this reason I make known to you that no one speaking by the Spirit of God says, "Jesus is accursed"; and no one is able to say "Lord Jesus" except by the Holy Spirit.
Now there are distributions of gifts of grace, but it is the same Spirit.
And there are distributions of ministries, and it is the same Lord himself.
And there are distributions of workings, and it is the same God himself, who works all things in all.
But to each one of us the manifestation of the Spirit is given for what is most beneficial.
To one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom, and to another the word of knowledge by the same Spirit,
and to another faith from the same Spirit, to another the gift of healings from that same Spirit,
to another workings of powers, to another prophecy, to another discernment of spirits, and to another various kinds of tongues, and to another interpretation of tongues.
But all of this is worked by one and the same Spirit, who distributes to each person individually as he wills.
Just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of that one body, though they are many, are still one body, so also is Christ.
For by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or gentiles, whether slaves or free; and we have all been given to drink into one Spirit.
For the body is not one member, but many.
If the foot should say, "Since I am not a hand, I am not of the body," is it for this reason not of the body?
Or if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body," is it for this reason not of the body?
If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the senses of smell be?
But now, behold, God has placed the members, each one of them, in the body as he willed.
But if all were one member, where would the body be?
But now there are many members and one body.
And the eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you"; or again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you."
But much more, those members of the body that are thought to be weaker are the more necessary.
And those parts of the body that we think to be without honor, to these we give greater honor.
And our unseemly parts have greater seemliness, while our seemly parts need nothing. But God has blended the body together and has given greater honor to the part that lacks,
so that there may be no division in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another.
And if one member suffers, all the members suffer with it; and if one member is glorified, all the members are glorified with it.
You are the body of Christ, and members of his members.
And some God has appointed in the churches: first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then powers, then gifts of healings, helps, administrations, various kinds of tongues.
Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all powers?
Surely not all have the gift of healings? Surely not all speak in tongues? Surely not all interpret?
But strive eagerly for these greater gifts, and further I will show you a surpassing way.
Though I speak with the tongue of men and of angels and have not love, I have become like brass that resounds or cymbals that clang.
And though I have prophecy and know every mystery and all knowledge, and though I have all faith, even to the moving of mountains, if I have not love, I am nothing at all.
And though I give away all my possessions as food and hand over my body to be burned, and have not love, it is of no profit to me at all.
Love is long-suffering and kind; love does not envy, love does not exalt itself, is not puffed up,
does not behave shamefully, does not seek its own, does not become angry, reckons no evil,
does not rejoice over falsehood, but rejoices over the truth;
it bears all things, believes all things, hopes in all things, endures all things.
Love never falls away, whether prophecies pass away, or tongues cease, or knowledge passes away.
For we know only in small part and we prophesy only in small part.
But when the perfect comes, then that small part will pass away.
When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I was reckoned as a child; but when I became a man, I left behind what belongs to childhood.
For now I see as through a mirror and in a figure, but then face to face; now I know in small part, but later I shall know as I have been known.
But now, behold, faith, hope, and love abide, these three; but greater than these is love.
Pursue love and strive eagerly for what is spiritual, but rather that you may prophesy.
For the one who speaks with a tongue speaks not to people but to God, for no one understands, since by the Spirit he speaks mysteries.
But the one who prophesies speaks to people edification, exhortation, and consolation.
The one who speaks with a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the assembly.

I desire for all of you the speaking of tongues, but rather that you may prophesy, for the one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the assembly may be edified.
But now, brothers, if I come to you and speak in tongues, how will I benefit you, unless I speak to you by revelation or by knowledge or by prophecy or by teaching?
So too lifeless things give out a sound, whether pipe or harp; if they do not give a distinction of sounds, how will the piping or the harping be recognized?
And if a trumpet gives out an indistinct sound, who will prepare for battle?
So also you: if through the tongue you do not give out an intelligible word, how will what is said be recognized? For you will be like people speaking to the air.
There are so many kinds of sounds in the world, and not one of them is without sound.
If then I do not know the force of the sound, I will be to the one speaking to me as another tongue, and the one who speaks to me will be as another tongue to me.
So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual gifts, seek them for the building up of the church, so that you may excel.
Therefore let the one who speaks in a tongue pray that he may also interpret.
For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.
What then is it? If I pray with the spirit, let me pray with the mind also; if I sing with the spirit, let me sing with the mind also.
But if you bless with the spirit, how will the one who occupies the place of the unlearned say "Amen" to your thanksgiving? For he does not know what you are saying.
For you indeed give thanks well, but your neighbor is not built up.
I thank my God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
But in the church I would rather speak five words with my mind, so that I may also instruct others, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
Brothers, do not be children in your thinking; be children with regard to evil, but in your thinking be mature.
For it is written in the Law: "With a foreign tongue and with foreign lips I will speak to this people, and even so they will not listen to me, says the Lord."
Therefore tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers; but prophecy is not for unbelievers but for believers.
Now if the whole assembly gathers together and all speak in tongues, and some unbelievers or unlearned people come in, will they not say, "You are in error," or "You are raving"?
But if all prophesy, and some unbeliever or unlearned person comes in, he is reproved by all, he is judged by all.
And so the hidden things of his heart are revealed, and so he will fall on his face and worship God and confess, "Truly God is among you."

What then is it, brothers? When you gather together, each one of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has an interpretation, has speaking in tongues: let all these things be done for building up.
If anyone speaks in a tongue, let there be two, or at most three, and let one interpret.
But if there is no interpreter, let them be silent in the church; let them speak to themselves and to God.
And let two or three prophets speak, and let the others discern.
If a revelation comes to another person sitting there, let the first one be silent.
For you are all able to prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be comforted.
And the spirits of prophets are subject to the prophets,
For God is not a God of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of the saints.
Let your women be silent in the church, for it is not commanded for them to speak, but to be in submission, as the Law also says.
But if they wish to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home; for it is shameful for women to talk in the church.
Or did the word of God go out from you? Or did it reach only as far as you?
If anyone thinks himself to be a prophet or spiritual, let him know that the things I am writing to you are the commandments of the Lord.
But if anyone is ignorant, let him be ignorant.
Therefore, my brothers, be zealous to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
And let everything be done beautifully and in order.
But I make known to you, brothers, the gospel which I preached to you, which you have received, on which you also stand,
by which you are also being saved, the word which I preached to you, if you remember it, unless you believed something in vain.
For I delivered to you first what I also received: that Christ died for our sins, as it is written,
and that he was buried, and that he rose on the third day, as it is written,
and that he appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve.
and then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at one time, most of whom are alive until now, and some have fallen asleep,
then he appeared to James, and then to all the apostles,
Last of all, as to a castoff, he appeared to me as well.
For I am the castoff among the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the churches of God.
But by the grace of God I am what I am; and his grace, which was toward me, was not in any way in vain, but I labored more than all of them; not I, but the grace of God that was with me.
Now therefore, whether I or they, thus we preach, and thus you believed. 9 [?]
But if Christ is preached, that he has risen from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not been raised either.
If Christ has not risen, then this preaching of ours is indeed in vain, and that faith of yours is in vain.
So we are also found to be false witnesses of God, for we testify concerning God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise, if indeed the dead do not rise.
For if the dead do not rise, neither has Christ risen.
And if Christ has not risen, that faith of yours is futile; you are indeed still in your sins until now.
And those who have fallen asleep through Christ have indeed perished.
If we hope in Christ in this life only, we are more pitiable than all people.
But now Christ has risen from the dead, and he has become the beginning of those who have fallen asleep.
For through a man came death, and through a man the resurrection of the dead.
And just as because of Adam all die, so also through Christ all will be made alive.
But each in his own order: first Christ, and then those who are Christ's at his coming.
Then comes the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when he has destroyed every rule and every authority and power.
For he must reign until he puts all his enemies under his feet.
Last, that enemy will be abolished: death,
for he has subjected everything under his feet. But when it says, 'He has subjected everything,' it is clear that this is apart from him who subjected everything to him.
But when everything is subjected to him, then the Son himself will also be subjected to him who subjected everything to him, so that God may be all in all.
Otherwise, what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead do not rise at all, why then are they baptized for the dead?
Or why are we in distress at every hour?
I die daily, I swear by my boasting in you, which I have through Christ Jesus our Lord.
If in human fashion I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what profit is it to me, if the dead do not rise? Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we shall perish!
Do not be deceived: evil counsels corrupt good customs.
Awake in righteousness and do not sin; for some have ignorance of God. I say this to your shame.
But someone will say: How do the dead rise, and with what flesh will they come?
Foolish one! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
And what you sow, you do not sow the body that is to be, but a bare grain, whether of wheat or of some other seed.
But God gives it a body as he wills, and to each seed its own body.
Not all flesh is one flesh, but there is one flesh of humans, and another flesh of cattle, and another flesh of birds, and another flesh of fish,
and there are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies; but the glory of the heavenly is one thing and that of the earthly is another.
There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for just as star surpasses star in glory,
So it is also with the resurrection of the dead: it is sown in corruption and rises in incorruption;
it is sown in dishonor and will rise in glory; it is sown in weakness and rises in power;
it is sown a natural body and rises a spiritual body. There is a natural body and there is a spiritual one.
So also it is written: The first man Adam became a living being, but the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
But the spiritual is not first, but the natural, and only then the spiritual.
The first man is from the earth, of dust; but the second man is the Lord from heaven.
As the one of dust was, so also are those of dust; and as the heavenly one is, so also are those of heaven.
And as we have put on the image of the one of dust, let us put on the image of the one of heaven.
But this I say, brothers: flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor shall corruption inherit incorruption.
Behold, I tell you a mystery: we shall not all fall asleep, but we shall all be renewed,
in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet; for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise incorruptible, and we shall be renewed.
For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
And when this corruptible puts on incorruption and this mortal puts on immortality, then the word of Scripture will be fulfilled: Death is swallowed up in victory.
"O death, where is your sting? O hell, where is your victory?"
For the sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the Law.
But thanks be to God, who has given us the victory through Christ Jesus our Lord.
From now on, my beloved brothers, be firm and unshakable, and abound in the work of the Lord. Know always that this labor of yours will not be in vain in the Lord.
Now concerning the offering for the saints, as I commanded the churches of Galatia, so you also are to do.
On each first day of the week, let each one of you set aside by himself and store up whatever he may prosper in, so that the collection will not be made only when I come.
And when I come, those whom you have approved by letters, these I will send to carry your gift of grace to Jerusalem.
And if it is fitting that I also go, they will come with me.
And I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.
And, who knows, perhaps I will stay with you or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way wherever I may be going.
For I do not wish to see you now just in passing; but I hope to stay some time with you, if the Lord commands us.
But I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost,
for a great and helpful door has been opened to me, and those who attack me are many.
And if Timothy comes, see that he is without fear among you, for he does the work of the Lord, just as I do.
So let no one despise him, and send him on to me in peace, so that he may come to me, for I am waiting for him with the brothers.
Now concerning Apollos the brother, I earnestly begged him to come to you with the brothers; and it was certainly not his will to come now, but he will come when he has the opportunity.
Be watchful, stand firm in the faith, be courageous and be strong.
Let everything of yours be done in love.
And I beseech you, brothers, for you know the household of Stephanas, that it is the first of Achaia, and they have appointed themselves to the service of the saints,
that you also submit to such people and to every fellow helper and laborer.
And I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, for they have filled up what was lacking on your part,
for they have refreshed my spirit and yours as well. Therefore acknowledge such people.
The churches of Asia greet you; Aquila and Priscilla greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the congregation that dwells with them.
All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
The greeting is by my own hand, Paul's.
Whoever does not love our Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. Maranatha.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus; amen.
